newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu seals accord on "Who is a Jew".
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu seals accord on "Who is a Jew".

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government said on Sunday it had signed an accord with Reform and Conservative Jews vowing to resolve their dispute with Orthodox Jews in Israel over "Who is a Jew".
Under a deal signed with Reform and Conservative representatives, Netanyahu promised to create a committee to draft a proposal that would satisfy "all parties".

Parliament approved preliminary legislation in April to enshrine in law a long-standing "status quo" whereby people converted in Israel to Judaism would be officially recognised as Jews only if the conversion was performed by an Orthodox rabbi.

Opponents said that bill, which passed the first of three readings, would alienate non-Orthodox Jews who make up the overwhelming majority of Jews in the United States, home to the world's largest Jewish community.
The legislation was part of a coalition deal between Netanyahu's ruling Likud party and religious factions.

Under the new deal a seven-member committee, including one representative each from the Reform and Conservative movements, will present its recommendations to Netanyahu's coalition by August 15 before going to parliament if required.

Coalition whip Michael Eitan said two months ago the preliminary legislation, approved by a vote of 51 to 32 with seven abstentions, would not be presented for its final readings until all efforts to hammer out a compromise were exhausted.
Government officials said Israel would in any event go on accepting as valid conversions done outside its borders by rabbis in the Reform and Conservative movements.
